2022.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.4.7

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

Media Player / Apple TV

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/apple_tv/

service: media_player.play_media
data:
  media_content_id: /Users/server/test.mp3

review_comments:
I don't think this is right? How would this handle signing for non-media sources now?

The reported issue is raising `ValueError("URL is relative, but does not start with a /")`, which is odd it raised in the first places. Where do these non-root relatives come from?

The issue I noticed was that if `media_id` is passed a local filename, e.g. /media/myfile.mp3, it would always get translated into a media source URL (https). That's why I feel it's wrong in the general case to call `async_process_play_media_url` , so I moved it.

I'm not following your logic on that one? It will translate it to `https` in case the relative URL is not explicitly allowed AND the internal URL isn't available (or the internal URL itself it set to `https`).

Isn't the solution to allow for relative URLs instead?

`async_process_play_media_url(self.hass, play_item.url, allow_relative_url=True)`?

Right, so it's not sent over as an URL to the device (which fetches and plays it), but instead, we try to open the file and stream its contents?

If so, why? as in, looking at the above, it can handle URLs?

Yeah, pyatv opens the file locally and streams it. Audio streaming with AirPlay is purely local. A receiver cannot pull stream a stream from a URL itself, a sender must stream audio packets to it. So streaming from a URL basically means that Home Assiatant serves a file that pyatv downloads (streams), decodes and sends to the receiver. That loop is very excessive when pyatv can just open the file locally instead. Also, streaming via HTTP is even more experimental than regular streaming from a file. It has a smaller buffer and less poorer error handling, so in reality I would prefer steaming over HTTP altogether.

> So streaming from a URL basically means that Home Assiatant serves a file that pyatv downloads (streams), decodes and sends to the receiver. That loop is very excessive when pyatv can just open the file locally instead.

So why do we generate URLs out of media sources in that case (which you moved and kept)?

> So why do we generate URLs out of media sources in that case (which you moved and kept)?

From what I have gathered, a media id can resolve to a local file (which is served via the web server, so it generates a URL) but it could also resolve to a URL by itself in case of it being a remote resource (like a URL to an Internet radio station for instance). So a media id must be resolvable for these cases. A local file would just be a local file and should not be resolved in any way. If a media id for a resource in the media library can be resolved to local file, then I would prefer to get the file path instead to avoid looping data over HTTP but still resolve in other cases and fallback to URL-based when nothing else is possible. Locally I have reverted the change and made it to resolve relative, but not pushed it (until I know it's actually supposed to be).

Media sources always resolve to URLs. If you know of a media source that doesn't, that's a bug and we should fix that.

If a media source resolves to a relative URL, it needs to be prefixed with the HA host. That's what `async_process_play_media_url` is for. 

If ATV supports local file paths, moving `async_process_play_media_url` into the browse media if-statement is correct. That way it will only apply to the output of resolved media sources and not accidentally to local file paths.

We suggest putting `async_process_play_media_url` outside of the if-statement to allow passing any relative HA URL to play_media and it works. In this case this move inside the if-statement is fine as we cannot distinguish between relative HTTP urls and file paths.
